Fix auto-updater to use build tags instead of broken semver parsing

Release tags use `build-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-SHA` format, but the update
checker was trying to parse them as semantic versions, causing all
update checks to silently fail. Now compares build tags directly,
embeds the tag in Info.plist during CI, and checks every 7 days
instead of 3. Also removes the debug settings tab.

Fix recording producing 0 audio buffers when Bluetooth headphones are connected

When Bluetooth headphones are connected, macOS creates a synthetic
CADefaultDeviceAggregate device that interferes with AVAudioEngine's
audio tap on the built-in microphone. The engine starts successfully
but the tap never delivers audio buffers, causing recording to silently
fail (stuck on initializing overlay, then transcription fails with
HTTP 400 on an empty WAV file).

This adds two recovery layers:

1. Proactive: Observe AVAudioEngineConfigurationChangeNotification to
   detect when macOS reconfigures audio (BT connect/disconnect). When
   fired during recording, transparently rebuild and restart the engine.
   On second attempt, fall back to the system default device.

2. Reactive: A 2-second buffer watchdog that detects when the engine
   starts but produces 0 buffers, triggering the same rebuild/fallback
   logic as a safety net.

Also fixes a pre-existing data race on bufferCount by wrapping it in
OSAllocatedUnfairLock, and refactors engine creation into a reusable
buildAndStartEngine() method.

When the active dictation binding is a modifier-only shortcut on the
SAME modifier key as the Edit Mode manual modifier (for example Right
Option as the toggle binding + Option as the manual modifier), every
press of the binding key produces a "modifier currently held" signal
that the manual command path treats as "user is holding the manual
modifier while pressing the dictation shortcut" — even though the
press IS the binding itself, with nothing else held alongside.

Without selected text, the path then routes through
rejectCommandModeSelectionRequirement, plays Basso, and refuses to
start dictation. Key-repeat amplifies the issue into a rapid-fire
Basso loop while the binding is held.

Repro:

  2. Settings → Edit Mode → Extra Modifier → Option
  3. Settings → Tap to Toggle → Right Option
  4. Click somewhere editable, no text selected
  5. Tap right option → Basso fires every ~300ms, no dictation starts

Fix: in the .manual case of intent resolution, before checking
manualCommandRequested, detect whether the active binding's keyCode IS
the manual modifier. If so, fall back to plain dictation — the
modifier-pressed signal is the binding's own press, not an additional
held modifier.

property surfaces the warning. setCommandModeManualModifier was the

  2. No warning fired, because the message was returned without the

  3. The computed validation property still saw the unchanged modifier

Mark checkForUpdates as @MainActor to avoid an NSAlert hang

UpdateManager.checkForUpdates(userInitiated:) is async but
UpdateManager itself is not @MainActor-isolated. After the
URLSession await, post-await code can resume on a background
executor. The function then calls showUpdateAlert() (or one of
the showUpToDate/showError variants), each of which calls
NSAlert.runModal() — which must be on the main thread.

Calling runModal from a background executor is undefined behavior
and on macOS Sonoma can hang waiting for an event loop that never
spins on that thread. When it hangs, defer { isChecking = false }
never fires because the function never returns. The Check for
Updates button stays in its disabled "Checking for Updates..."
state forever, with no error and no alert.

The fix is a single @MainActor annotation. URLSession's async API
still releases main during the network wait, so this is not a
UI-blocking change. All callers already invoke from @MainActor
context (SwiftUI Button action closures and the periodic-check
Task { @MainActor in ... } handler).

Close recording overlay panel on dismiss

orderOut(nil) only hides the overlay panel. AppKit retains every
ordered-in window in NSApp.windows until it is closed, and dismissAll()
drops its reference without closing, so each dictation leaks a hidden
panel with its NSHostingView hierarchy still mounted. Anything live in
that hierarchy keeps running — the processing indicator's repeatForever
spinner keeps driving Core Animation transaction flushes, and the
initializing-dots timer never receives onDisappear.

Profiled at 6-7% sustained main-thread CPU and growing memory after
normal dictation use; a 5-second sample showed CA::Transaction::commit
and NSWindow layout driven by RepeatAnimation with zero visible
windows. After this change the main thread returns to fully idle once
the overlay dismisses.

Unmount the content view and close the panel so it deallocates.
isReleasedWhenClosed is already false, so close() is safe.

Add tolerance to the hourly update-check timer

A repeating Timer with no tolerance forces the system to wake at the
exact scheduled instant, defeating timer coalescing. The hourly update
re-check does not need precision — shouldAutoCheck() already gates on
elapsed time since the last check — so a 5-minute tolerance lets macOS
batch the wakeup with other system work and reduce idle power draw.

Apple's Energy Efficiency Guide recommends tolerance of at least 10% of
the interval for repeating timers; 300s on a 3600s timer follows that
guidance.

Add setting to keep dictations in clipboard history

Dictated text is marked transient/concealed unconditionally, so clipboard
managers (Maccy, Raycast, Paste, etc.) always skip recording it. That is the
right default for most users, but some rely on clipboard history as a recovery
buffer: when an auto-paste lands in a non-text field (common in Electron and
Chromium apps where the focused element is not exposed via the accessibility
API), the transcript is otherwise only recoverable via Paste Again.

Add a 'Keep dictations in clipboard history' setting, default off so current
behavior is unchanged. When enabled, the transcript is written without the
transient markers so clipboard managers record it. Wired through the same
points as preserveClipboard: storage key, published property, initializer,
the pasteboard write, and a Clipboard settings toggle.

Distinguish network outages from slow-provider timeouts in transcription errors

When a transcription request fails, the error message shown to the user was the
raw system `localizedDescription`. For a dropped connection that surfaces as
"The Internet connection appears to be offline." — technically accurate, but it
reads like an app bug and buries the actual cause.

Two changes fix this:

- A small `NetworkMonitor` (a long-running `NWPathMonitor`) tracks reachability
  so a request timeout can be told apart from a genuine outage. A hung socket
  trips the request timeout and otherwise looks identical to a slow provider.

- Transcription errors are now classified by the locale-independent
  `URLError.Code` instead of matching the system's English description, which
  varies across releases and locales. The underlying-error chain is walked so a
  wrapped transport error is still classified by its root cause. Connectivity
  failures collapse to a single clear "No internet — check connection"; a
  timeout while still online stays "Request timed out — try again".

The monitor starts once at launch and is read-only on the hot path, so there is
no added cost to a successful dictation.

Commit settings text editors on focus loss to fix typing lag

The Custom Vocabulary, System Prompt, and Context Prompt editors wrote
their value into the shared AppState on every keystroke. Because AppState
is a single ObservableObject observed by the whole settings window and the
menu bar, each keystroke fired objectWillChange and rebuilt all of those
views. On a macOS 13 target there is no per-property observation to scope
the invalidation, so typing in these fields was noticeably laggy
(measured around 85ms of main-thread work per keystroke, with the menu bar
rebuilding on every character).

These fields now commit to AppState when the editor loses focus, matching
what the API base URL and key fields already do, and also on disappear so
nothing typed is lost if the window closes while focused. The prompt test
runners commit first so they still test the latest text.
